per_case_results.query: As a central government employee, how is the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation determined?
per_case_results.direct_answer: For a Central Government employee, the perquisite value of unfurnished government-provided residential accommodation is determined as the License Fee fixed by the Central Government under its rules, minus any rent actually paid by the employee. If the accommodation is furnished, the value is increased by 10% per annum of the original cost of furniture/appliances owned by the government (or actual hire charges if rented), reduced by any furniture charges paid by the employee.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Applies as per Rule 3 amendments effective from September 1, 2023 (relevant for Financial Year 2023-24 / Assessment Year 2024-25 onwards).

per_case_results.query: I am a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income. Can I submit a declaration to my bank under Rule 26D so that no tax return is required to be filed?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Yes, as a 77-year-old senior citizen receiving pension and interest income, you can submit a declaration in Form No. 12BBA (in paper form duly verified) to your specified bank under Rule 26D of the Income-tax Rules, 1962. Once you furnish this declaration along with evidence of Chapter VI-A deductions, the bank will compute your total income, allow eligible deductions and Section 87A rebate, and deduct the appropriate tax under Section 194P, exempting you from the requirement to file an income tax return.

per_case_results.query: I changed jobs during the previous year. What form must I submit to my current employer to declare salary and TDS from my previous employer under Rule 26A?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 26A of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, you must submit either Form No. 16 or Form No. 12BA to your current employer, depending on the amount of salary paid from your previous employer. If the total salary from the previous employer is ₹1,50,000 or less, you file Form No. 16. If it exceeds ₹1,50,000, you file Form No. 12BA along with your income tax return (ITR).
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: This applies to the Financial Year (FY) 2019-20 and Assessment Year (AY) 2020-21 under the Income-tax Rules, 1962. The effective date of Rule 26A is not specified (None), so it has been in continuous operation since its introduction under the 1962 regime.

per_case_results.query: How did the Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption rules change between Rule 2B of the 1962 rules and Rule 278 of the 2026 rules regarding block years?
per_case_results.direct_answer: The LTC exemption rules evolved significantly between the 1962 and 2026 regimes. Under the 1962 rules (Rule 2B), the exemption was available for travel concessions received during a block of four calendar years, with the right to claim the amount in the first year of the next block if not utilized previously. The 2026 rules (Rule 278) introduced stricter limitations including a cap of two surviving children per individual for the exemption, a specific Rs. 30 per km calculation method for non-rail connections without recognized public transport, and explicitly limited the exemption to two journeys within a block of four calendar years starting from 2022.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Both the 1962 Rule 2B and 2026 Rule 278 are currently in force with no effective date restrictions noted in the provided statutory context. The 2026 rules specifically reference the financial year/calendar year 2022 onwards, while the 1962 rules apply retroactively to relevant periods.

per_case_results.query: Can a salaried individual claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) under Goods and Services Tax (GST) for office suits purchased from salary?
per_case_results.direct_answer: No, a salaried individual cannot claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) under GST for office suits purchased from their employer. GST ITC is only available for purchases from GST-registered vendors, not from employers or personal sources. Office suits purchased from an employer are not eligible for GST ITC as they fall under the category of wages/salary, which are exempt from GST and do not generate GST liability for the purchaser.
